review.summary: The diff swaps the retired Groq model IDs for openai/gpt-oss-120b and openai/gpt-oss-20b in the UI, the model choices list and the webhook fallback. The model IDs are not in my knowledge, so I could not confirm them. The quoted source names only the retirement, not the replacements, so check them against the deprecations page. The main gap is persisted data: users who saved a prompt config with a retired model keep that value. promptModel.ts passes `promptData.model` straight to runGroqChat, so those users' webhooks will fail after 2026-08-16 and the diff does not touch them. Typecheck and build only prove the strings compile. The model-proof check going from fail to pass is the only runtime-ish signal, and I can't tell how it validates models. The 'verified' grade looks somewhat generous given the stored-config gap. Separately, gpt-oss models are reasoning models, which may affect output and token usage, and may not suit the `temperature: 0.2` setting or the existing prompts. That's unproven. Pre-existing: promptModel.ts has an unused module-level `groq` client and passes `ownerGithubId` as userId in the fallback path, unlike the custom path.

concerns.issue: The custom-prompt path uses `promptData.model` from the DB. Existing rows with llama-3.1-8b-instant or llama-3.3-70b-versatile will still be sent to Groq after shutdown and fail. No migration, mapping or fallback was added.
`activeConfig?.model` is still used as the first choice for the test tab, so users with a stored retired model will hit errors. The new default only applies when no model is set.

The select list no longer contains the old values, so stored configs with the old models may render as blank or unmatched in the model selector. The `restricted` flags were carried over without confirming plan gating still fits the new models.

I could not confirm openai/gpt-oss-120b and openai/gpt-oss-20b as valid Groq IDs from memory. They are reasoning models, so response content, latency, token usage and handling of `temperature` may differ from Llama. Nothing here tests that behaviour.
Only the replacements for the two named models were applied. The deprecation notice says there are 8 changes, and other retired models may still be referenced elsewhere in the repo.
